beats.lead: OpenAI's image generator is named after a robot and a surrealist painter.
beats.text: DALL·E is a portmanteau of Salvador Dali, the Spanish surrealist, and WALL-E, Pixar's 2008 robot.
beats.note: OpenAI never spelled the joke out in dry technical language; the pun was already the headline when NBC News covered the launch.

beats.text: OpenAI published DALL·E on 5 January 2021: a 12-billion-parameter version of GPT-3, retrained to generate images from text captions instead of continuing text.
beats.note: The model treats an image as 1,024 extra tokens tacked onto a caption's 256, then predicts all of them the way GPT-3 predicts words.

beats.text: For every caption, DALL·E generated 512 candidate images, then used a second model called CLIP to rerank them down to the best 32.
beats.note: OpenAI stated none of its published examples were hand-picked beyond that automatic reranking.

beats.context: parameters in the original DALL·E, a fraction of GPT-3's full size, repurposed entirely for pictures.

beats.text: DALL·E turned out to be able to translate images the way GPT-3 translates text: performing image-to-image tasks it was never explicitly trained on.
beats.note: OpenAI's own paper says: "We did not anticipate that this capability would emerge, and made no modifications to the neural network or training procedure to encourage it."

beats.line: Named for a robot and a surrealist. Launched 5 January 2021.
